preamble: Seven solutions are of a kind and may lack further definition.

clue.text: Preventer of leak used to be female

explanation.surface: Someone who once plugged leaks was apparently a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a little sentence: WAS HER, 'used to be her', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is the small ring fitted in a tap or joint to seal it and stop drips escaping.

clue.text: Setter's crying out loud for sweet

indicators.note: something said out loud is heard, so the spelling may differ from what reaches the ear

parts.note: the setter says 'I', and crying is screaming

explanation.surface: The setter is wailing in a craving for something sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of a crossword refers to themselves as 'I'. The old rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream' plays on the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is a pudding or dessert course, and a frozen dairy dessert qualifies.

clue.text: Confine sovereign under tree on field in Shaftesbury

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming after it in the column

parts.note: a ley is a meadow or field of grassland
to coop up is to confine

explanation.surface: Instructions to fence in a monarch beneath a tree on a meadow in the Dorset town of Shaftesbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree on field' puts ASH above LEY; 'confine sovereign' comes under them. Shaftesbury is a Dorset town, but here it is the earldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashley-Cooper is the family surname of the Earls of Shaftesbury, notably the Victorian social reformer Anthony Ashley-Cooper.

clue.text: Translate from French: tobacco healthy, dessert fatal

indicators.note: to translate is to carry something over into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A health warning in reverse: tobacco is fine, but the pudding will kill you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translate from French' looks like an instruction to render a phrase into English; instead 'from' in French supplies two letters to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a rich chocolate pudding jokingly claims it is lethal, so it is a dessert described as fatal.

clue.text: Promoter of chaos with a spanner

parts.note: the indefinite article in its other form

explanation.surface: A troublemaker armed with a wrench, ready to throw it in the works.
explanation.walkthrough: A spanner here is not the tool but anything that spans, such as the curved structure of a bridge. 'Spanner in the works' adds to the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarch is an old word for an anarchist, someone who seeks to overthrow order and authority.

clue.text: Doctors abandon oxygen

parts.note: MO is a medical officer; plural

explanation.surface: Medics give up on supplying oxygen to a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay; the preamble's 'of a kind' supplies the definition. The seven are Second World War RAF aircraft, and the de Havilland Mosquito was a fast wooden bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Mosquito was a wartime British combat aircraft, one of the seven thematic planes in this grid.

clue.text: Way with throw-in to right?

indicators.note: something put in goes inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a lane is a road or way

explanation.surface: A footballer asks which direction to take a throw-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw-in' is football language for restarting play, but here it splits: a throw goes in the way. The Avro Lancaster was the RAF's best-known wartime heavy bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avro Lancaster was a four-engined British bomber of the Second World War, one of the thematic aircraft.

clue.text: Pole coming in presently

indicators.note: arriving inside means one piece enters and sits within another

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor will arrive shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a person from Poland, but it is a magnetic pole, here the southern one. The Avro Anson was a twin-engined wartime trainer and patrol plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avro Anson was a British aircraft used for reconnaissance and training in the Second World War, matching the theme.

clue.text: See 4
Arab brains turned after change of air

indicators.note: coming after means being placed later in the sequence
a change of something alters it, so its letters are rearranged
turned round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: intelligence quotient, a measure of brains

explanation.surface: A clever Arab's mind changed once the climate did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brains' is the measure of intelligence, IQ. 'Change of air' sounds like a holiday, but it means scrambling the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, an Arab nation, so the nationality noun is an instance of an Arab.

clue.text: A lot of larks mean drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the collective noun for a flock of larks
second meaning: an old sense, a drink or drinking bout, kin to beverage

explanation.surface: Having larks, or fun, means drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Larks' suggests pranks and fun, but these are the birds. The drink sense is also close to the British slang 'bevvy', an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, especially of larks or quails, and in older use a drink, from French for a drinking.

clue.text: How to cook fish inside without having to pay

indicators.note: something inside is held within, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: frying is a way to cook

explanation.surface: A recipe tip for fish served at a free meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to cook' is the cooking method, not instructions; the fish goes inside that method word.
explanation.definitionFit: Done freely means given at no cost, gratis, so something obtained without charge.

clue.text: Fight for an apple

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1704 battle won by Marlborough in Bavaria
second meaning: an English dessert apple variety, the '... Orange'

explanation.surface: Two people squabble over an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Also a thematic answer: the Bristol Blenheim was an RAF light bomber. Blenheim Palace was built for Marlborough after the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The battle gives the word as a fight; the Blenheim Orange is a cultivated dessert apple named after the palace.

clue.text: One minute's silence for the French museum man

parts.note: a mo is a moment; the possessive just ties it to the silence

explanation.surface: A minute's silence held for a French museum curator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One minute's silence' reads as a tribute, but the pieces are separate. Elias Ashmole founded the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias Ashmole was the 17th-century collector whose gift founded Oxford's Ashmolean, Britain's first public museum.

clue.text: High church feature: object to female intruding

indicators.note: something intruding pushes its way inside, so pieces go within another

parts.note: a tall pointed structure on a church
it is the pronoun for an object

explanation.surface: A church feature, and an objection to a woman barging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High church' suggests the Anglo-Catholic wing, but it is just a tall church. 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest; it is a noun. The Supermarine Spitfire was the RAF's famous fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supermarine Spitfire was the iconic British fighter of the Battle of Britain, one of the thematic aircraft.

clue.text: Troops in 11's rhyme

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soldiers raised by conscription
second meaning: a word rhyming with the answer to 11 down

explanation.surface: Soldiers chanting a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 11 down is BEVY; change its first letter for a rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a body of soldiers called up or conscripted, so the word can stand for troops.

clue.text: Person without energy — former minister

indicators.note: being without something means lacking it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a type is a kind of person, as in 'not my type'
Geoff Hoon, a British Defence Secretary under Tony Blair

explanation.surface: A worn-out ex-minister, out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Hoon was UK Defence Secretary until 2005, aptly for an aircraft theme. The Hawker Typhoon was an RAF fighter-bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker Typhoon was a British ground-attack fighter of the Second World War, one of the thematic aircraft.

clue.text: _____ ? Then wear a woolly hat!

parts.note: surface reading: a blank to fill, some ailment that a hat would help
setter's reading: the blank is literal advice, a chilly top of the body calls for a hat

explanation.walkthrough: Read the missing words literally: if your head is cold, a woolly hat is the cure. The phrase actually names a sniffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold is a common illness of the nose and sinuses, and the clue treats the phrase as literal chill.

clue.text: Heavy defeat in scam leaves one in the soup

indicators.note: something in another is held within it

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A crushing loss in a swindle leaves someone in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble; here it is literal, a thing floating in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread served floating on top of a bowl of broth.

clue.text: Find record complete

explanation.walkthrough: 'Record complete' sounds like a finished log, but it is a vinyl disc and a word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon or locate it, a direct synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: See 3
Big pot given to gossip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an Indian earthenware water jar
second meaning: talkative, fond of idle talk

explanation.surface: A self-important person who loves to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big pot' suggests a bigwig, an important person; it is a literal pot, a word from Anglo-Indian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty (or chatti) is a large porous clay pot from India; as an adjective it means talkative and gossipy.

clue.text: Former president on the wagon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jimmy, US president 1977 to 1981
second meaning: a driver sitting on a cart

explanation.surface: A past head of state who has given up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' is an idiom for teetotal; the question mark tells you to take it literally, someone riding a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Carter was a US president, and a carter is someone who drives a horse-drawn cart for hauling goods.

clue.text: Householder permitted article under canvas?

indicators.note: something under cover is enclosed by it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas

explanation.surface: Is a homeowner allowed to camp?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' means camping; the question mark flags that the article literally goes inside the camping shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant occupies a house by the owner's permission, paying rent rather than owning the property outright.

clue.text: What's going on in the Yard?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the three twelve-inch units that make up a yard

explanation.surface: A question about what is happening at Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital Y makes it Scotland Yard; the answer splits as a measure, three of which make the length unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is in progress or being planned, while a single foot sits within the length of a yard.

clue.text: After a lot of haste I get to stick

indicators.note: a lot is most but not all, so the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: Rushing about only to end up stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb, to become stuck; it is a walking stick. The Hawker Hurricane fought alongside the Spitfire in the Battle of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker Hurricane was a British single-seat fighter of the Second World War, one of the thematic aircraft.

clue.text: Unintelligible participant in tug of war

definitions.note: adjective, as in 'it's Greek to me'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in 'it's all ... to me', of incomprehensible talk
second meaning: from an old proverb about two evenly matched rivals pulling against each other

explanation.surface: A competitor in a rope-pulling contest whom nobody can understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'When Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war' describes two equally matched rivals clashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is incomprehensible is called Greek, and the old saying pits one Greek against another in a struggle.

clue.text: Add weight here for a thematic eighth — it will dry

parts.words: Add weight here for a thematic eighth
parts.note: setter's reading: put a weight word into this answer and rearrange to reach an eighth wartime aircraft, the Vickers bomber named after the Iron Duke
surface reading: a fabric used for drying

explanation.surface: Weight training talk alongside a cloth for drying.
explanation.walkthrough: The eighth plane is the Vickers Wellington, absent from the grid: add N, a newton, to the answer and rearrange, or swap its opening TO for TON, a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Towelling is absorbent terry cloth from which bath sheets are made, so it is a material whose job is drying.
